jobs.title: Director, AI Strategic Initiatives
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where tech thinkers and future builders turn bold ideas into breakthrough experiences, we welcome your unique perspective.

Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriers—because progress starts with fresh ideas. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

We are seeking a Director of AI Strategic Initiatives to lead the development and delivery of technically complex AI solutions that solve business problems and advance strategic AI capabilities. This role combines deep AI expertise with business judgment and execution ownership. You will identify opportunities, define solutions, and work closely with Engineering, Product, and business teams to move initiatives from technical validation through enterprise integration and production deployment. The scope includes AI solutions embedded in enterprise workflows, specialized language models, persistent agents, and capabilities such as agent identity and security. It also includes exploring AI-enabled products and services with Product and commercial leaders.

Responsibilities

Solve Business Problems Through AI

Partner with business leaders to identify specific problems where AI can deliver measurable value
Assess technical feasibility, data readiness, integration requirements, and expected business impact
Translate business needs into solution requirements, technical approaches, and delivery plans
Define success measures and remain accountable for results through deployment and operational use

AI Solution Development and Delivery

Drive initiatives from problem definition and prototyping through evaluation, integration, and production delivery
Guide the design of solutions using generative AI, predictive models, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic systems
Work with engineering teams to integrate solutions across enterprise applications, data sources, and workflows
Evaluate build, buy, and partnership options, with clear recommendations on cost, capability, and long-term fit
Resolve technical and delivery barriers, manage dependencies, and bring decisions to the appropriate owners

Advance Strategic AI Capabilities

Identify and validate emerging AI approaches with practical enterprise or commercial applications
Lead selected initiatives involving small and specialized language models, persistent agents, and multi-agent systems
Partner with platform, architecture, and security teams on agent identity, authorization, secure tool access, and lifecycle controls
Establish reusable solution patterns that extend the enterprise AI platform and accelerate subsequent delivery

Lead Cross-Functional Execution

Establish clear ownership, milestones, and delivery commitments across business and technical teams
Ensure solutions align with enterprise data and AI architecture, security, privacy, and governance requirements
Partner with the AI Transformation team to bring technical solutions into broader value-stream programs where appropriate
Communicate progress, results, risks, and decisions clearly to senior leaders

Build and Lead the Team

Lead and develop a team with strong AI solution design and technical delivery capabilities
Set a high standard for technical judgment, engineering quality, and execution
Maintain sufficient hands-on involvement to challenge designs, evaluate prototypes, and guide difficult technical decisions

Qualifications

12+ years of experience in AI/ML, data science, or related engineering disciplines, including significant technical leadership experience
Experience leading technically complex initiatives across engineering, data, product, and business teams
Experience integrating AI into enterprise applications and workflows
Ability to assess emerging technologies and turn promising approaches into practical solutions
Strong business judgment, including prioritization, investment tradeoffs, and build-versus-buy decisions
Ability to connect technical decisions to business outcomes and explain tradeoffs clearly
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills
Experience in maintaining accountability across organizational boundaries

jobs.title: Director, Portfolio Management & Governance
jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

We are looking for a Director, Portfolio Management & Governance within the Technology Project Management Office.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance reports to the AVP, Program Management & Governance and is accountable for the integrated planning, governance, and delivery oversight of technology investments within the Canada Operations & Business Enablement portfolio. The Director works closely with senior business and technology leaders to establish priorities, evaluate investment trade-offs, manage portfolio-level risks and dependencies, and ensure initiatives deliver measurable business value within approved financial and capacity constraints. The role leads a team of Program Managers and Project Managers and serves as a trusted advisor and escalation point for portfolio delivery.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance is outcome-focused and capable of leading high-profile, highly complex, or ground-breaking programs of work while providing clear, credible advice to senior leadership.

What you will do:

Planning:

Lead the development of the annual portfolio delivery plan and budget within Technology, and work with business partners to refresh a multi‑year delivery roadmap that aligns with strategic priorities.
Collaborate with Technology and Business Portfolio Leaders to assess and socialize priorities, ensuring visibility into impacts across systems, processes, and other portfolios.
Support the creation of an integrated cross‑portfolio delivery plan by aligning project investments with business and technology strategies.
Partner with divisional leadership to identify resource needs and staff programs and projects with appropriately skilled team members.
Work closely with Technology leaders to define priorities, objectives, scope, and deliverables that support enterprise goals and desired business outcomes.

Delivery Oversight & Governance:

Oversee the successful delivery of complex technology programs and projects within the assigned portfolio, ensuring alignment to business value, timelines, and budget.
Analyze incoming demand and structure it into programs, projects, or epics as appropriate.
Apply appropriate Governance Frameworks to guide business case development and ensure required documentation and approvals are in place.
Lead and develop a team of Program Managers and Project Managers accountable for delivery execution.
Conduct regular program retrospectives and post‑implementation reviews to drive continuous improvement and capture lessons learned.
Manage portfolio‑level risks and issues, ensuring effective analysis, mitigation, communication, and resolution.
Synthesize portfolio performance, financial forecasts, risks, dependencies, and delivery outcomes into clear, concise, and decision-oriented communications for senior leadership and governance forums. Proactively surface emerging concerns, articulate business impacts, and recommend practical courses of action.
Maintain detailed portfolio‑level spend plans and ensure strong financial governance across all initiatives.
Serve as the escalation point for all delivery‑related issues, risks, decisions, and changes within the portfolio.
Manage resource capacity, workload balancing, and team assignments to ensure optimal delivery performance.
Apply the most appropriate delivery methodologies—Waterfall, Agile (Scrum/Kanban), Hybrid, etc.—to achieve optimal business outcomes, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards and methodologies.

What you will bring:

A university or college degree in a relevant field.
A minimum of eight years of progressive technology delivery experience within financial services, insurance, fintech, or a comparably complex organization, including at least three years leading multi-million-dollar programs, portfolios, or enterprise initiatives. Experience with application development and technology modernization is preferred.
Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders, influencing outcomes with confidence and credibility.
Proven executive-level communication skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio, delivery, financial, and risk information into clear, concise, decision-oriented messages for senior leaders. Demonstrated experience preparing and delivering executive presentations, facilitating governance forums, influencing senior stakeholders, and communicating difficult issues or recommendations with confidence, sound judgment, and appropriate transparency.
Demonstrated portfolio management experience, including investment planning, prioritization, financial forecasting, capacity planning, dependency management, and the evaluation of competing initiatives against business value and strategic outcomes.
Proven ability to apply sound judgment and constructive challenge within governance forums, including testing assumptions, identifying gaps, escalating concerns, and helping senior leaders make informed investment and delivery decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing delivery professionals, including setting clear accountabilities, coaching performance, building succession capability, and creating an environment of transparency, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Ability to work across organizational boundaries and influence business and technology leaders with competing priorities, building alignment around enterprise outcomes rather than optimizing for a single project, function, or portfolio.
A strategic mindset with the ability to evaluate programs through the lens of business value and enterprise outcomes.
Strong comfort with ambiguity and change, with the ability to navigate uncertainty by seeking clarity from diverse stakeholders and available information.
Exceptional multi‑tasking and prioritization skills, thriving in a fast‑paced and demanding environment.
A passion for building, developing, and empowering high‑performing teams; a leader who models continuous learning, innovation, and an entrepreneurial mindset.

annually. This represents base salary only and does not represent other variable compensation components of our total compensation ( i.e. annual bonus, commission etc). jobs.title: VP, Global Finance Risk / Prime Services Risk
jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

We are looking to bring on a VP into our Global Finance Risk team, to be based out of the Toronto office.

This person will be responsible for managing risk across prime, counterparty credit, and business and developing the risk framework, which includes margin risk methodologies. The person will also collaborate across teams, including trading, credit, market risk, counterparty, and the front office to work cohesively and collaboratively to ensure all risk coverage. They will also be responsible for stress testing and scenario analysis for the business.

The role provides direct risk oversight of a business supporting sophisticated counterparties and structured financing activity. Responsibilities extend beyond routine monitoring and require both technical risk expertise and sound judgment.

The resource would be expected to:

Support the counterparty and platform risk management of BMO’s cash and synthetic Prime Brokerage and Equity Delta One business lines
Solutions-oriented client engagement throughout the lifecycle of a client
First line of defense in risk managing credit risk and monitoring platform exposure
Generation of key risk analytics and development of new tools to support insights and emerging risk trends
Understanding market and credit risks within Prime products and effectively communicating to senior management and control functions
Evolving the risk framework and other risk governance items to ensure a proper control environment and strategic platform development
Support senior team members in responses to Regulatory inquiries and periodic requests
Key in-business coverage for emerging counterparty risk events and crisis management
Contributes to growing / elevating the BMO and BMO Capital Market Prime Brokerage brand with a commitment to and presence in the community
Balances the Bank's risk appetite with the client needs in making recommendations/proposals
Manages firm’s risk and takes action to reduce exposure in developing and delivering client strategies
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Job Background / Context:

Global platform includes Prime Brokerage and Swap offerings across US, Canada and the UK.
Client portfolios comprise of a broad range of asset classes and investment strategies, including: Equities (incl. Common Stock, ETFs, ADRs, MLPs, REITs), Corporates (IG & HY), Convertible Bonds, Options & Indexes
Hedge fund and real money counterparties

Key Responsibilities:

Daily management of client portfolio exposures and counterparty-related risk issues
Support of operational risk and platform trade processing associated with client counterparty risks
Participation in prospective client pitches and term negotiations, modeling commercial risk terms and constructing incentives to support strategic, risk-efficient returns growth through ongoing client dialogue
High level of engagement with Sales, Trading and other members of the business as it relates to client management and ongoing business initiatives
Thoughtful and complete analysis and communication of risk concerns both internally within the business and among control function partners
Identifying and escalating emerging risks – credit, market, operational or legal – to senior management and Global Finance management. Continuously assessing and adapting to new products and market stress events and proactively proposing risk solutions
Facilitating new client trades and managing existing portfolio exposures to ensure that risks, primarily market-driven counterparty risk, but also documentation, legal and reputational risks are well-controlled
Work closely with Counterparty Credit, Credit Risk Management and other key stakeholders on onboarding of new clients, implementation of margin methodology, as well as maintaining ongoing dialogue and promptly escalating issues with existing clients
Develop strategic risk solutions, analytics and platform enhancements to help advance BMO’s competitive advantage
Maintain a positive culture within the team by cultivating a productive and collaborative work environment
Ensure full compliance with risk procedures and other Global Finance or Global Markets policies

Qualifications:

B.S. – Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Finance / Statistics or related discipline.
Between 5 - 7 years of experience in Prime Finance risk or general experience with Delta One and Global Prime Finance trading
Experience with VaR and stress testing.
Strong data querying and quantitative analysis skills are required, knowledge of Python, SQL and AI Development tools.
Comfort with using data querying skill set to design risk dashboards, graphic user interfaces linked to internal databases and enhanced risk reporting.
Exposure to and strong understanding of equities products, such as Delta One, Swaps, and derivatives across all asset classes. Experience with Synthetic Prime is a plus.
Strong understanding of market risk and counterparty risk processes and metrics.
Knowledge of relevant Prime financing platforms, asset types, market structure and client investment strategies.
Experience with data infrastructure transformation, financial engineering and/or quantitative expertise in risk modeling / data analytics.
Experience with risk decision-making authority carrying direct economic impact.
Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth.
Collaboration & team skills - In-depth.
Analytical and problem solving skills - In-depth.
Influence skills - In-depth.

jobs.title: Director, Application Services
jobs.description:
Beem Credit Union: Banking for every journey

Beem is redefining what it means to be a credit union. With 80 years of cooperative history and a bold vision for the future, we’ve united to create a financial partner that offers both digital ease and people-first service.

Our mission is clear: financial wellness for all.
We help British Columbians achieve their goals through personalized advice, innovative technology, and genuine human connection.

As one of BC’s largest credit unions, we serve over 200,000 members
across 66 branches
with $18 billion in assets under administration
.

If you’re passionate about making a difference and want to join a team that values collaboration, innovation, and purpose, join us on the journey.

Learn more: www.beemcreditunion.ca

What this role is all about:

Reporting to the VP, Digital Solutions, the Director, Application Services
is a senior technology leader accountable for the health, reliability, performance and ongoing evolution of Beem’s enterprise-wide Application Services portfolio, which includes core banking, lending, digital banking, enterprise applications, and other assigned business applications. The role ensures these applications remain secure, resilient, current and well supported, providing a dependable and scalable foundation for Beem’s members, employees and business operations. The Director sets the multi-year strategic direction for Application Services and owns the operating model, investment priorities and portfolio decisions within their accountability, shaping how applications are managed and evolved across Beem.

The Director leads multiple teams responsible for application support, configuration, upgrades, patching and testing, operational vendor management, and delivery of small non-material enhancements. The role translates Business and Technology priorities into coordinated application service and lifecycle plans, balancing operational excellence with application simplification, automation, responsible AI and continuous improvement to reduce friction, improve efficiency and enable Beem’s digital-first and people-first ambitions.

This is a hybrid position, and preference will be given to applicants located in British Columbia. In-person interview(s) will be required during the later stages of the recruitment process, with location(s) to be determined.

What you’ll do:

Leadership and Team Success

As a member of the Technology Leadership team, accountability for the decisions connecting application services priorities to member outcomes, business needs and Beem’s strategic direction.
Leads Beem’s Application Services portfolio, building high-performing teams and establishing clear accountability and service ownership across the applications, while fostering collaboration, curiosity and continuous improvement.
Owns the Application Services operating model, organizational structure, budget, and service ownership model, including the allocation of leadership accountability across teams and managers, and evolves the model as Beem’s application portfolio and strategic priorities change.
Builds workforce capability in application service management, digital platforms, automation and responsible AI, supported by coaching, career pathways, succession planning and knowledge sharing.
Aligns team capacity and skills to operational commitments, lifecycle requirements and approved change priorities, making trade-offs visible and escalating constraints before delivery or service is affected.
Maintains sustainable support coverage, including extended-hours and on-call arrangements for critical services, while reducing key-person dependencies and supporting employee well-being.

Application Services & Operational Resilience

Owns the operational health of applications in scope, establishing service expectations and monitoring that reflect business criticality, member journeys and employee needs.
Leads application incident and problem management in partnership with Technology Operations, the Service Desk and vendors, restoring service promptly and addressing root causes to prevent recurrence.
Oversees application configuration and administration, including product and rate setup, workflows, business rules and in-application access, supported by appropriate approvals, testing and controls.
Strengthens application observability, runbooks, known-error records and knowledge practices to identify issues earlier and improve first-contact resolution.
Partners with business continuity, disaster recovery and Technology teams to validate application recovery readiness, test critical dependencies and address resilience gaps.

Application Lifecycle & Change Delivery

Develops and maintains an enterprise-wide rolling multi-year application service and lifecycle roadmap aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture and technology plans, balancing currency, resilience, supportability and cost.
Provides recommendations on application consolidation, retirement and standardization to reduce duplication, technical debt and operational complexity, with investment and architecture decisions made through established governance.
Leads vendor upgrades and patches through impact assessment, regression testing, cutover and stabilization, maintaining visibility into version currency, end-of-support exposure and remediation plans.
Delivers configuration changes and small enhancements on non-material initiatives, coordinating dependencies, release readiness and stakeholder communication to minimize member and employee disruption.
Establishes mandatory operational acceptance criteria for new or materially changed applications and has authority to withhold operational acceptance where service readiness, resilience, supportability or control requirements have not been met.

AI, Automation & Continuous Improvement

Develops and prioritizes a practical improvement backlog using service data, incident trends and member and employee feedback, focusing on reduced friction, reliability and measurable operational value.
Introduces approved AI-enabled and automated practices for activities such as ticket triage, knowledge management, release analysis and regression testing, with human accountability and appropriate oversight.
Partners with business owners, Enterprise Transformation & Integration, and Technology teams to translate process improvements into supportable application changes, while preserving clear business, delivery and operational accountabilities.
Measures whether improvements reduce manual effort, recurring demand and service delays, and redirects released capacity toward higher-value work and priority commitments.

Business Partnership, Risk & Vendor Management

Partners with business and product teams to understand how application services enable everyday banking, digital engagement and advice-led relationships, translating those needs into clear operational priorities.
Collaborates with Architecture, Information Security, Infrastructure and Operations, Engineering, and Data teams to manage application dependencies and support consistent, reliable experiences across channels.
Owns and manages operational vendor relationships, holding providers accountable for service commitments, issue resolution, release coordination and transparent escalation.
Responsible for application cost, usage and service insights to support budget planning, procurement decisions and vendor assessments.
Maintains visibility into application risks, control gaps and remediation commitments, providing decision-ready reporting on service health, lifecycle exposure, vendor performance, capacity and improvement outcomes.
Owns remediation commitments for application risks and controls gaps for their portfolio.

A little about your qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology, Engineering or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
10+ years of progressive experience in application support, application management or IT service delivery, including senior people leadership experience.
Deep experience supporting business-critical applications in financial services, ideally including core banking, lending and digital banking platforms.
Strong grounding in service management practices, including incident, problem, change and release management; ITIL certification or equivalent experience is an asset.
Proven experience managing application vendors, service-level performance, escalations and upgrade coordination.
Demonstrated success planning and delivering application upgrades with disciplined regression testing and minimal member impact.
Experience with AI-enabled or agentic applications in production, or a strong interest in building this capability, including monitoring, evaluation and responsible change control.
Understanding of operational resilience, risk and control expectations within a regulated financial institution.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across business and technical partners.
Working knowledge of modern service management and monitoring tools, such as ITSM platforms, application monitoring and observability tools, Azure DevOps or Jira.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Total Rewards:

Our total rewards approach reflects Beem's values — celebrating success, investing in your growth, and supporting you at work and in life.

Compensation: Annual salary range of $151,100 - $188,900, with pay based on your skills and experience, and performance bonuses tied to shared goals
Health & Wellness: Extended health coverage (including mental health support), dental care, and disability coverage
Time Away: Vacation and personal days to rest, recharge, and manage life outside of work
Retirement & Financial Well-being: Generous RRSP contributions, in-house financial advice, and flexible options to add your own contributions
Beem Member Perks: Free banking accounts, special mortgage and lending rates, and preferred financial perks

At Beem we are BOLD and Always Welcoming and our values are at the forefront of everything we do!

Build Together: You are a team player who thrives on collaboration, sparks ideas, and fosters inclusivity.
Own It: You are ready to take charge, drive change, and deliver outstanding results.
Lead with Agility: You are a dynamic, adaptable thinker who thrives on challenge and innovation.
Driven by Curiosity: You are eager to explore, learn, and shape the future.

Ready to join?

Visit us at www.beemcreditunion.ca to learn more about what it’s like to work for Beem Credit Union! We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

We at Beem Credit Union are committed to ensuring inclusive employment practices and an accessible business environment for our employees. We do not discriminate based on any protected attribute covered by the Human Rights Code and encourage all qualiﬁed candidates to apply. We are committed to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates. All applications are reviewed by a member of our team.

At a glance

Location: Montréal, QC. Hybrid, with about half your time on-site.

About Nomic

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Our story began at McGill University, where our co-founders and early team developed breakthrough technology that would change the way proteins are measured.

Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. For the first time, large-scale, quantitative proteomics is accessible to any scientist, supporting everything from drug discovery and translational research to AI-enabled therapeutic development.

Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

Learn more in our Series B announcement.

The role

As Director, Supply Chain, you will oversee end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, logistics, and inventory management. You will drive the development and execution of strategies to optimize performance, reduce costs, and improve reliability across systems and workflows. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams to align production schedules, streamline material flow, and mitigate supply risks. You will also lead data-driven forecasting, manage supplier relationships, and establish clear metrics to monitor and continuously improve supply chain effectiveness. This role is ideal for someone with a strong track record in a high-growth environment, particularly in life sciences, and experience operating at the intersection of manufacturing and services.

What You’ll Do

Procurement

Own our material and product costs within our standard cost model, analyzing cost structure and inventory variances and leading improvements in cost efficiency.
Design and maintain procurement workflows that are scalable, automated and audit-ready, including for materials used in quality-controlled processes.
Develop sourcing strategies and manage supplier relationships, from negotiation to ongoing performance oversight.
Work with Sales, Manufacturing and Service Lab leaders to forecast material needs, using data-driven models and increasingly automated tools.

Sales and operations planning

Lead materials and supply planning with operational leaders, aligning production plans, raw material supply, inventory and supplier capacity with the sales forecast.
Build and maintain operational and capacity models that support resource planning and budgeting.
Own our ERP as its subject matter expert: data integrity, accuracy and how well it serves the business.

Inventory

Own our inventory systems and processes, with tight integration between the ERP and Nomic’s internally developed LIMS, the central hub for our operational data.
With your peers, set inventory carrying strategies that balance operational performance and financial stewardship.
Oversee receiving: intake, verification and system entry of inbound materials.
Keep physical inventory accurate across all storage sites, including temperature-controlled storage, and own material movement, reconciliation and audit readiness.
Track raw materials, work in progress and finished goods end to end, including lot traceability and shelf life.

Logistics

Build and run outbound logistics for our kit business: order fulfillment, packaging, shipping, temperature-controlled distribution, delivery tracking and returns.

What You’ll Bring

You’re naturally curious, quick to learn and energized by solving problems with people across disciplines. You think end to end, from planning and procurement to inventory and logistics, and you want to design systems that work well and scale from day one. You bring an engineering mindset, you’re comfortable with technology, and you care about making things run smoothly, reliably and transparently. You approach operations practically and iteratively, always looking for the next improvement.

You’ve seen what good looks like in a fast-growing manufacturing organization like ours. You know when to move fast, when to push back and when to step in and fix something yourself. You adapt how you work with others, handle change and ambiguity well, and colleagues trust you to bring structure without rigidity. You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

Relevant experience. 7+ years in supply chain, operations or manufacturing roles supporting manufacturing. Life-science tools experience is strongly preferred; we also welcome candidates from other industries with strong technical adaptability.
Leadership and building experience. Experience leading and developing people. Building scalable processes in a high-growth company or having led a supply chain function is a plus.
Procurement and cost expertise. Experience owning strategic sourcing and supplier negotiations, and working with standard costing and variance analysis. Experience developing procurement practices in a quality-controlled environment is a plus.
Planning and inventory experience. Experience connecting sales forecasts to production and materials planning, with ownership of manufacturing inventory control. Experience shipping temperature-controlled goods is a plus.
ERP expertise. Subject matter expertise in an ERP system; NetSuite is highly desirable.
Cross-functional communication. You work effectively with scientific, operational and commercial teams and can turn complex requirements into practical processes.
Education. An advanced degree (for example an MSc) in engineering, the life sciences or a related technical field is a plus.
Location. You can work on-site in Montréal about half the time. Working proficiency in French and English is an asset.

Why join us

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.

Nomic a été fondée pour faciliter la mesure biologique et permettre aux scientifiques de prolonger la vie en rendant la protéomique accessible, évolutive et courante. .

Vous dirigerez également les prévisions fondées sur les données, gérerez les relations avec les fournisseurs et établirez des indicateurs clairs pour suivre et améliorer continuellement l'efficacité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Ce poste conviendra parfaitement à une personne qui a fait ses preuves dans un environnement en forte croissance, en particulier dans les sciences de la vie, et qui a l'habitude d'évoluer à la jonction de la fabrication et des services.

Vos responsabilités

Assumer la responsabilité des coûts de nos matériaux et de nos produits dans le cadre de notre modèle de coût standard, en analysant la structure des coûts et les écarts d'inventaire et en dirigeant les initiatives d'amélioration de l'efficacité des coûts.

You’ve built dashboards. Tracked milestones. Chased vendors. Flagged risks. But your reports hit a ceiling. You weren’t the one making the calls.

2 Hour Learning is building an AI-powered education model designed to help students achieve a full day of academic progress in just two hours. Making that model work at scale requires dozens of initiatives, technology partners, contracts, and investment decisions to move in sync. Your job is to make the execution layer trustworthy enough for executives to act on it.

You will own the operating outputs behind those decisions: portfolio dashboards that expose slippage before it becomes a surprise, vendor scorecards tied to real contractual commitments, competitive bid packages that make trade-offs clear, and contract controls that prevent unsupported spend. AI will be part of your daily workflow, helping you standardize updates, detect anomalies, compare bids, analyze vendor performance, and validate invoices.

This is not a PMO role built around meetings, process compliance, or polished status decks. It is for an operator who wants their work to have consequences. When a vendor underperforms, your evidence should make that obvious. When spend drifts from the contract, your controls should catch it. When executives need to make a $5M decision, your outputs should give them the confidence to make it fast. If that sounds like the level of ownership you have been looking for, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Own portfolio-level dashboards across 10+ concurrent initiatives, using AI to standardize updates, detect slippage, expose blockers, and maintain a trusted executive view of delivery, budget, and risk
Run recurring vendor performance reviews and maintain rubric-based scorecards that combine delivery, quality, cost, contractual commitments, and qualitative performance signals
Lead competitive technology-vendor procurement, including structured bid packages, normalized comparisons, scoring rubrics, SOW development, and evidence-backed recommendations
Govern contracts and invoices by tracking fee caps, milestones, acceptance criteria, and amendments, then validating invoices against signed terms before spend is approved
Use AI daily to analyze portfolio data, detect anomalies, surface underperformance, draft decision-ready outputs, and reduce manual PMO administration

What You Won’t Be Doing

Producing status reports that executives read but never use to make decisions
Running a meeting-heavy PMO where coordination matters more than measurable execution
Treating vendor management as relationship maintenance while missed commitments go unchallenged
Passing contracts, SOWs, invoices, or procurement decisions to someone else because they look too commercial or technical
Using AI as an occasional productivity trick instead of a core part of how you operate

VP Portfolio Operations Key Responsibilities

As VP Portfolio Operations, you will produce reliable, AI-powered dashboards, scorecards, procurement packages, and contract controls that give executives the clarity and leverage to hold vendors accountable, control costs, and accelerate delivery across a $50M EdTech portfolio.

Basic Requirements

Personally owned execution across 10+ concurrent initiatives with at least $5M in portfolio budget responsibility, tracking spend and making evidence-backed recommendations on budget allocation, vendor selection, and initiative priorities. Final approval authority and P&L ownership are not required
Managed 5+ external technology vendors at the same time, such as SaaS providers, AI/ML platforms, marketing agencies, or engineering firms
Built and maintained portfolio-level dashboards covering metrics such as delivery health, budget burn versus forecast, milestone completion, and major risks or blockers
Can point to a case where C-suite leaders used your portfolio data to make a go/no-go decision on a vendor renewal, budget reallocation, or initiative deprioritization
Directly led competitive technology procurement, including structured bid evaluation, vendor scoring, negotiation, and recommendations for executive approval
Authored or co-authored SOWs with measurable deliverables, milestone payments, SLAs, acceptance criteria, or other performance-based terms
Negotiated commercial terms such as pricing, penalties, fee caps, or exit clauses and enforced those terms through invoice validation or corrective action
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn complex financial and operational data into concise recommendations executives can act on
Able to analyze financial and vendor-performance data quickly enough to recommend optimization, reallocation, or vendor elimination
Able to work US business hours

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience using AI-enabled dashboards, anomaly detection, predictive alerts, or natural-language analysis in portfolio management
Experience in EdTech, technology, consulting, or another environment managing complex portfolios of external technology partners
Fluency with portfolio and delivery tools such as Linear, Jira, or similar systems

About 2 Hour Learning

Education is broken, but 2 Hour Learning is proving it doesn’t have to be. They’re tearing down the outdated one-size-fits-all model and replacing it with AI-driven personalized learning that helps kids master academics in just two hours a day.

With students consistently ranking in the top 1-2% nationally and the top 20% achieving an astonishing 6.5x growth, they’re proving that smarter learning is possible. At 2 Hour Learning, it’s talent and performance that matter.

They offer a dynamic, on-campus and remote-friendly environment where innovators, educators, and AI specialists can be a part of fixing a broken school system.

2 Hour Learning is reprogramming learning for the AI era.

Here’s How They’re Fixing It.

About Nomic

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Our story began at McGill University, where our co-founders and early team developed breakthrough technology that would change the way proteins are measured.

Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. For the first time, large-scale, quantitative proteomics is accessible to any scientist, supporting everything from drug discovery and translational research to AI-enabled therapeutic development.

Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

Learn more in our Series B announcement.

The role

As Director, Supply Chain, you will oversee end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, logistics, and inventory management. You will drive the development and execution of strategies to optimize performance, reduce costs, and improve reliability across systems and workflows. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams to align production schedules, streamline material flow, and mitigate supply risks. This role is ideal for someone with a strong track record in a high-growth environment, particularly in life sciences, and experience operating at the intersection of manufacturing and services.

What You’ll Do

Design and maintain procurement workflows that are scalable, automated and audit-ready, including for materials used in quality-controlled processes.

Own our ERP as its subject matter expert: data integrity, accuracy and how well it serves the business.

Inventory

With your peers, set inventory carrying strategies that balance operational performance and financial stewardship.
Oversee receiving: intake, verification and system entry of inbound materials.
Keep physical inventory accurate across all storage sites, including temperature-controlled storage, and own material movement, reconciliation and audit readiness.
Track raw materials, work in progress and finished goods end to end, including lot traceability and shelf life.

Logistics

Build and run outbound logistics for our kit business: order fulfillment, packaging, shipping, temperature-controlled distribution, delivery tracking and returns.

You’re naturally curious, quick to learn and energized by solving problems with people across disciplines. You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

ERP expertise. Subject matter expertise in an ERP system; NetSuite is highly desirable.

Location. You can work on-site in Montréal about half the time. Working proficiency in French and English is an asset.

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.
